title: Twisted-arrow graph comparison is coinitial
statement:
Use quasicategories, nerves, mapping spaces, coherent functor categories and colimits of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], the twisted-arrow construction $\operatorname{Tw}$ and its projection $\lambda$ of [lem-coef-twisted-arrow-left-fibration], and classification of left fibrations by space-valued coherent functors of [lem-coef-space-valued-straightening]. Let $f:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be a functor of quasicategories in a common sufficiently large universe $\mathcal V$. Define the simplicial pullback
$$W_f=(\mathcal B^{\mathrm{op}}\times\mathcal A)\times_{\mathcal B^{\mathrm{op}}\times\mathcal B}\operatorname{Tw}(\mathcal B),$$
using $1\times f$ on the first factor and $\lambda$ on the second. Its projection to $\mathcal B^{\mathrm{op}}\times\mathcal A$ is the left fibration classified by the coherent mapping-space functor $(x,a)\mapsto\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal B}(x,f(a))$, with the latter formed in the infinity category of $\mathcal V$-small spaces, in a larger ambient universe. The simplicial map
$$\kappa_f:\operatorname{Tw}(\mathcal A)\longrightarrow W_f$$
is induced by $(f^{\mathrm{op}}\times1)\lambda$ and $\operatorname{Tw}(f)$; at an arrow $a\to a'$ it is the triple $(f(a),a',f(a\to a'))$. Its opposite $\kappa_f^{\mathrm{op}}$ is final: in every containing target universe, for every quasicategory $\mathcal E$, diagram $p:W_f^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal E$ and $e\in\mathcal E$, restriction induces an equivalence
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(W_f^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal E)}(p,\Delta e)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(\operatorname{Tw}(\mathcal A)^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal E)}(p\kappa_f^{\mathrm{op}},\Delta e).$$
Thus any specified cocone on $p$ is colimiting if and only if its restriction is colimiting, with the same vertex. The pullback, classification and graph map are natural in commutative squares of functors $f$. In particular, if $\mathcal A$ is $\mathcal U$-small for a smaller universe $\mathcal U$, the domain $\operatorname{Tw}(\mathcal A)^{\mathrm{op}}$ is $\mathcal U$-small, even if $\mathcal B$ is not.
